reason: All five mandatory audit matrix checks (MATRIX-001 through MATRIX-005) have been completed by their assigned agents across RUN-0002 through RUN-0006, with a cross-run synthesis completed in RUN-0008. The corpus now contains substantive findings across hardware, risk traceability, software, DMR/SOP, and regulatory dimensions. However, several high-severity cross-cutting issues identified across multiple agent runs require consolidation and inter-agent cross-verification before the audit can be closed or escalated to human review. Specifically: (1) the Bluetooth hazard gap was independently flagged by Risk Traceability Agent, Software Agent, and V&V Agent but no single agent has been tasked to consolidate and determine whether any Bluetooth verification evidence exists anywhere in the corpus; (2) the version mismatch between PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 (cited in verification records) and V2.0 (active risk report) was flagged by both Risk Traceability Agent and V&V Agent and requires a focused cross-document traceability recheck; (3) the biocompatibility sample identity issue (PT5 samples used for PT9L reports) flagged by Regulatory Agent requires Hardware Agent confirmation against design output and BOM records; and (4) the unsigned approval fields systemic finding requires DMR/SOP Agent to confirm whether the design transfer record and design output list are also unsigned, completing the document-control closure picture. One additional cross-cutting synthesis assignment is warranted to produce a consolidated finding register before human review.

assignments.review_focus: Bluetooth hazard traceability closure check. Three independent agents (Risk Traceability Agent RUN-0003, Software Agent RUN-0004, V&V Agent RUN-0007) have each reported absence of Bluetooth-specific hazard identification, risk control, and verification evidence. This recheck must: (1) search the full corpus for any document referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in the context of PT9L hazard analysis or risk controls; (2) determine whether the Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0) contains a Bluetooth hazard entry and whether any corresponding verification record closes that control; (3) confirm whether the absence is a true gap or whether evidence exists in documents not yet retrieved; (4) assess whether the Bluetooth feature described in the project profile (PT9L transmits temperature to smart device via Bluetooth) is reflected anywhere in the ISO 14971 risk assessment chain. Do not confirm or dismiss the gap — locate and report all available evidence.

Risk document version alignment in verification records. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and V&V Agent (RUN-0007) both flagged that the design verification plan/report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk management report is V2.0. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design verification plan/report and identify every location where PT9L-FXGB01 is cited, recording the version number cited at each location; (2) retrieve PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 and identify what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 — specifically whether any risk controls added or modified in V2.0 have corresponding verification activities in the verification plan/report; (3) determine whether any change record, amendment, or addendum to the verification plan/report acknowledges the V2.0 update; (4) assess whether the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities is broken by this version mismatch. Do not render a finding verdict — locate and report all available evidence.

Biocompatibility sample identity cross-check against BOM and design output records. Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) flagged that biocompatibility reports were conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the biocompatibility report(s) and identify the sample description, part numbers, and product model cited in the test sample section; (2) cross-reference those sample part numbers against the PT9L EBOM (PT9L-EBOM01) and any PT9L hardware design output drawings to determine whether the tested samples are materially equivalent to PT9L production parts; (3) identify whether any material equivalence justification or sample bridging rationale document exists in the corpus; (4) check whether the PT5 designation corresponds to a predecessor model or a sub-assembly designation within the PT9L product family. Do not confirm or dismiss the finding — locate and report all available evidence.

Unsigned approval fields — design transfer record and design output list completeness. Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006 and RUN-0008) identified a systemic finding of unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents. DMR/SOP Agent (RUN-0005) identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design transfer record and confirm whether approval, review, and release signature fields are populated or blank; (2) retrieve the design output list (both versions if two exist) and confirm the specific fields that are blank versus populated; (3) check whether any separate design review meeting minutes, ECO records, or approval routing records exist in the corpus that could serve as the approval evidence even if the document header fields are blank; (4) determine whether the process instruction referencing EBOM without version pinning also lacks an approval signature. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.

F0013 product-identity conflict resolution and IFT-prefix document number scope. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and Regulatory Agent (RUN-0006) both flagged that F0013 (a PT2L risk plan filed in the historical folder) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, and that the active Risk Management Plan carries an IFT-FXJH01 prefix rather than PT9L-FXJH01. This recheck must: (1) retrieve F0013 and record the exact internal document number shown on the document face, the document title, the product model referenced in the scope section, and the folder path where it is filed; (2) retrieve the active Risk Management Plan and record both the file name and the internal document number on the document face; (3) determine whether IFT is a recognized document-control prefix in the PT9L DHF (e.g., appears on other active documents) or is unique to this file; (4) assess whether any document index or master document list reconciles the IFT-FXJH01 identifier to the PT9L DHF scope. Do not confirm or dismiss findings — locate and report all available evidence.
